sentences.text: Scientists currently know Denazinosuchus only from parts of the skull, protective armor plates, and a single thigh bone.
Carl Wiman first described this animal in 1932 under the name Goniopholis kirtlandicus using skull material.
In 2003, Spencer G. Lucas and Robert M. Sullivan redescribed the species and elevated it to the new genus Denazinosuchus.
Denazinosuchus belongs to the family Goniopholididae.
It is classified as a goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian, a group within the class Reptilia.
Fossils of Denazinosuchus come from the Upper Cretaceous Fruitland and Kirtland Formations in the San Juan Basin, New Mexico.
This reptile lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
A 2025 phylogenetic study by Platt and colleagues recovered Paarthurnax as the sister taxon to Denazinosuchus.
